newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian PM seeks new government, ready to quit.
newsitem.headline: Estonian PM seeks new government, ready to quit.

text.p: Estonian Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi began talks on Tuesday to bolster his government a day after narrowly winning a no-confidence vote. He said he was prepared to quit if a better formula eluded him.
The opposition no-confidence motion failed by a vote of 46 to 45 in the 101-seat parliament on Monday.
Vaehi is leading the fifth government since Estonia regained its independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991 but has come under the shadow of corruption allegations.
His administration is a minority government with the definite support of 41 parliamentarians and five or six independents.
"We need a government which has majority support in parliament. I have started negotiations to form such a government," Vaehi said in a statement.
"If in order to find the best possible solution for Estonia it is necessary to nominate a new prime minister, I will not hesitate for a moment to hand in my resignation," he added.
Opposition parties moved the no-confidence motion after they alleged that Vaehi had helped privatise prime chunks of real estate in central Tallinn in an unethical manner.
They said that as head of Tallinn city council in 1993-1995 he arranged or knew that prime real estate was sold on the cheap and regulations were abused. Vaehi denied any wrongdoing.
Vaehi said that Estonia needed a stable government as key decisions were due to be made in the next six months on whether the country would be admitted to the European Union (EU).
Estonia is in a long queue with other former Communist bloc states to join the EU and believes it has a good chance of entering the trading bloc in a first round of expansion.
But Vaehi insisted he would not step down until agreement had been reached on an effective government.
"I will do everything so that a solution can be found very soon," Vaehi added.
